neighbours.label: determiner or possessive in Christian doctrinal text, in the slot before a title of Christ or God
fire: The letter to the Hebrews teaches that we draw near to God through Jesus the great high priest.
Peter preached that salvation is found in no other, for Christ is the cornerstone of the faith.
We worship the Father, and we confess that our Lord Jesus is the only begotten Son.
By his blood on the cross we are reconciled to God through the Lamb who was slain.
Paul tells the believers in Ephesus that Christ is the head of the church.
All things were made through Him, and we know the Creator by the works of His hands.
The tabernacle symbolises for Christians the priestly ministry of the risen Lord in heaven.
The Greek word Christos means the anointed one, the promised Saviour of Israel.
quiet: The letter from the council says that we reach the hall through the side door by the car park.
The vicar announced that the jumble sale is on Saturday, and the proceeds go to the roof fund.
The choir meets on Thursday, and we practise the new hymns in the church basement.
By the end of the service the pews were full and the flowers had been moved.
Paul tells the builders in Ephesus that Marcus is the head of the crew.
All the chairs were made in Leeds, and we know the carpenter by the marks on the legs.
The museum displays for visitors the bronze coins of the late Roman empire in a case.
The Greek word thalassa means the sea, the salty water around the islands.
